memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'You may ask, "What will we eat in the seventh year if we do not plant or
harvest our crops?" I will send you such a blessing in the sixth year that
the land will yield enough for three years'" - Lev 25:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God anticipates the honest question before Israel even asks it: what will
we eat? And He answers with a promise — the sixth year would produce
enough for three years.

Notice that God does not scold them for asking. He takes the question
seriously and answers it. Our God is not offended by our honest fears; He
meets them.

But notice also how the provision came. God did not remove the need to
trust. He gave a bumper harvest in the sixth year — before the year of rest
— so that they had to gather it, store it, and then live off it through the
fallow year while it seemed foolish to everyone around them. Faith was
still required.

Dear friend, this is often how God provides. Sometimes He gives ahead of
time, so we must trust what He has already supplied rather than what we can
currently see coming in. The manna in the wilderness worked differently —
daily — but the principle of dependence was the same.

Jesus taught us to pray, give us today our daily bread (Matt 6:11). Paul
promised that God is able to bless you abundantly, so that having all you
need, you will abound in every good work (2 Cor 9:8).

God sees the seventh year coming in your life. He is not caught off guard
by your future need.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What future need am I anxious about?
2. Can I trust that God already sees it and is preparing provision?
3. Has God already given me something I am failing to trust Him with?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that You see my needs before I voice them and provide
ahead of time. Help me trust Your provision even when it makes no sense to
those around me. Amen.
